# W34: The overlap shares against a public upstream source, and the failure segmenter reads the cluster check
**GitHub issue:** none; a file ticket, never published as an issue
**Status:** draft
Brief:
Add the contamination overlap shares of PREREG section 19 for a submission against its public upstream source (item 38c), and make the failure segmenter fail a run-cluster reply whose cluster check says `fail`.
Where: `src/distbench/overlap.py` (new), `tests/test_overlap.py` (new), `src/distbench/failure/segment.py`, `tests/test_failure_segment.py`.
Done means: `overlap.shares` gives share 1.0 for the upstream file itself, also with its whitespace changed, below 0.1 for an unrelated C file, about half for a half copy, and the registered n-gram length, denominators, file rule and new-n-gram share on token texts; `python -m distbench.overlap` prints both shares for a file or folder and exits 2 on a missing path; `segment.check_results` fails an `ok` reply whose `cluster_check` verdict is `fail`; every trace row due by batch 2 that names W34 has a check; the gate stays green.
Out of scope: freezing the codebook, the gold-set run, reporting the shares beside each port's score (W55, batch 3), any trace row.
Track: B    Risk: low    Mode: build    Open question: none
Work item: W34 of the implementation plan, section 6.2, batch 2 (U15 failure tools): its factory part; runs: the Loam factory from `~/distbench-isc`; Proven: D.
Base: `isc-build@a15f43056393c59836e0d54d7283a68ff5618776` (group 2 landed, U15 included; tip as last fetched on the Mac, 10 Nov); the run's real base is the round-0 sha in its `factory.log`, which must hold W07.
Size: 3-5 agent-hours (estimate: the plan's 4-8 h for the item, less the codebook and the gold set, which wait; the module is about 50 lines and the segmenter change one condition).
Blocked by: W07, J06, J08

## Goal and why
Item 38c keeps both public experts of the Jacobi and weather ports, with an overlap check of every submission against the public file reported beside every score (ledger V-tasks-26); this ticket builds the tool to the method the registered protocol already fixes (`docs/research/2026-10-12-fresh-design/PREREG.md` section 19, "The contamination overlap check"), and W55 (batch 3) calls `overlap.shares` on each port submission and reports its return.
U4's runner keeps a run-cluster job's status `ok` when the package's oracle rejects its output, adding the C5 verdict `cluster_check` (one of C5's verdicts) and an OUTPUT_MISMATCH finding; that runner part lands with group 5, so build to C5's reply shape, not to live runner output; so today the segmenter counts that job as a passed check and opens no failure episode (U15's open assumption).
Ledger ids closed: none in the plan's W34 entry; the build session's J06 gives V-tasks-26 a trace row for W34.
Trace ids its checks prove: item38c, and the docs/tickets/trace.tsv row `W34` (added by J06 at `ee9bf021`, on `isc-build` since group 21).

## Do not touch
The standing list.
Also: `tasks/`, `agent/`, `experiments/`, `pyproject.toml`, `src/distbench/failure/labels.json`, `src/distbench/failure/coders.py`, `tests/fixtures/failure_gold/`.
Except: `src/distbench/overlap.py` and `tests/test_overlap.py` (this ticket creates them).

## Out of scope
Freezing the codebook's labels, prompt template and shell-episode rule: the codebook entry, which the lead drafts in N6 (W42) for Samyak, freezes them.
Running the gold set against `tests/fixtures/failure_gold/BAR.md`: it waits for the two outside coders Samyak names, and an attended worker runs it then.
Reporting the overlap beside every port score (W55, batch 3), and editing docs/tickets/trace.tsv (J06 added W34's row).
Any pilot transcript (FREEZE).

## Approach
Build PREREG section 19's method as it is written, and read that section first.
`distbench.overlap.shares(submission, upstream, given)` takes three dicts of relative file path to text (the graded workspace S, the public version P, the package's `given/` G; W55 passes them so) and returns `{"share": |S & P| / |S|, "new_share": |(S - G) & P| / |S - G|}`, a share with an empty denominator `None`.
Each side is the set of its 13-token n-grams over its files whose names end in a suffix the section lists (`.c`, `.h`, `.cc`, `.cpp`, `.cxx`, `.hpp`, `.cu`, `.f`, `.f90`, `.F90`, `.py`); each file is split by `re.findall(r"\w+|[^\w\s]", text)`, comments and strings kept, and n-grams do not cross files.
`python -m distbench.overlap SUBMISSION UPSTREAM [GIVEN]` reads each as one file, or as a folder whose files at any depth form that side, `.distbench/` left out (GIVEN absent: an empty G), each file read as UTF-8 with errors replaced, and prints one line `share <3 places or null> new_share <3 places or null>`; it exits 2 with one stderr line when a path cannot be read.
Standard library only.
In `segment.check_results`, a reply whose status is `ok` and whose `cluster_check` verdict is `fail` gets the status `cluster_check fail`, so its check fails and opens or extends an episode; any other verdict leaves the status as it is; update the module docstring's rule.
Each new test that proves a trace row carries `pytest.mark.proves("<id>", fails_on="a15f4305", symptom="<what a15f4305 shows>")`: `item38c` on the overlap tests, and `W34` on one of them when the base's docs/tickets/trace.tsv has a row whose id is `W34` (it has since J06 landed on `isc-build` in group 21; a marker naming a missing row fails the trace check).

**Working rules when the work gets hard** (TOOLKIT section 5).
- Fail first: before the first edit, run every done check or Acceptance command on the base commit or planted edit this ticket names, and keep the output.
  Each non-guard check must fail with the symptom the ticket predicts, and each regression guard must give the base result the ticket records; any other result is a ticket defect: stop and report it, and never edit the check.
- Diagnose: for a failure whose cause you do not know, read `principle-fix-root-causes` and build the smallest command that fails on it, off the pair and the GPU when it reproduces there.
  Write that command and its output down before any fix, and fix the first place the state goes wrong, not the symptom.
- Stuck: when two fixes resting on one premise fail the same check, read `principle-attack-the-premise` and test the premise itself before a third attempt.
  In a factory run, consult the advisor tool before the third attempt; if the check cannot be met, write `ABANDON NAME reason` in decisions.md and stop.
  Attended, after a third failure on one item, stop and give the lead the evidence; the lead may rerun at xhigh or brief `escalate`.
- Second opinion (attended): before a choice that is costly to undo (a contract shape, a public interface, a frozen-check edit, one of several designs), ask the lead for a blind read by Codex read-only or `escalate`, given the artifact and its constraints, never your reasoning.
  When the same infrastructure failure returns after one fix, or the approach costs more than the goal is worth, ask the lead for a surprise-me pass aimed at this ticket's goal.
- Prove: prove a runner, agent command, package, oracle, orchestrator or grader change with `.agents/skills/verify-distbench/SKILL.md`, driving the real command line beside a control that fails.
  A change to a function `.agents/skills/formal-orchestrator/SKILL.md` maps runs its `tlc-check` and follows its DRIFT steps.
  Read `principle-prove-it-works` before you say done, `blast-radius` on a runner, grader or orchestrator change, and `benchmark-checklist` before you report any time.
  In a factory run these proofs live in the done checks, because your own shell is sandboxed.
  A step run on a stand-in (the local executor, a fake backend, the Mac) stays UNVERIFIED until it runs on its real target.
- Evidence: keep each command with its exit code and output in this ticket's evidence folder; in a factory run the supervisor's check output and decisions.md are the evidence, so mark anything they do not show as unverified.
  Long or live work keeps a `show-me-your-work` decision log; report under the seven headings of `docs/WORKERS.md`, ending with a READY line (host, exit code, log path).
- Never: edit, weaken or route around a done check or anything under `docs/tickets/checks/`; push or merge `main`; rent or make a paid call; launch a factory run (the lead does); kill a process by name or pattern; run a GPU, Docker or MPI job on jhaveris without its `flock` lock; open a FREEZE file.
- pstack: the router (`sam-cc-setup:pstack`) picks the method; a factory ticket's `skills:` line names only a skill that overrides its pick.

## Decisions
Fail first: the three overlap checks fail because `src/distbench/overlap.py` does not exist; `cluster-check-fail` reads `ok ok` (a `fail` verdict passes); `trace-rows` names item38c, closer W26 and W34, with no check; `check-green` is a regression guard.
Predict lines: at the Base commit `trace-rows`'s exits 1 (no bin/check_trace.py there), so round 0 refuses a base without W07; on the stand-in every predict exits 0.
J08 (on `build/w04-gate`) changes the line `bin/check` prints for pytest tests that did not run; before it lands, the factory judge reads the old line as a gate step that did not run and fails `verified`, so this run waits for it.
The unrelated file comes from another program, because another CoMD file shares much of CoMD's code.
The plan's done check (1.0 for the file itself, below 0.1 for an unrelated one) also passes for a score that only tests equality, so `overlap-partial` and `overlap-cli` pin a graded share; `overlap-bounds`' token texts pin the 13-token n-grams, the submission-side denominator, the new-n-gram share, n-grams not crossing files, the suffix list, the tokenizer, comments kept and sets rather than counts, and `overlap-cli` pins the file and folder inputs, GIVEN, the suffix filter, `.distbench/` left out and the UTF-8 reading; a 12-token n-gram, an upstream-side denominator, a reader of every suffix, counted n-grams, a whitespace tokenizer or dropped comments each fails one of them (ticket review, 11 Nov, on scratch scorers).
The method is PREREG section 19's, registered before the study, so it is not this ticket's choice (the draft's containment of the upstream's 5-grams departed from it, and only Samyak may change a registered rule); `shares` is the interface W55 calls. The lead's choices: the plan's codebook and gold-set parts left out (Out of scope); W07 in Blocked by for the trace check.
J06 landed on `isc-build` (groups 21 and 23); its trace rows include `W34`, which this ticket's marker names.
Held-out case: none.

### How we build
> **How we build (DistBench ISC build, rulings of 10 Nov 2026, items 27-58).**
> - Iterate to a correct version; there are no internal gates, and the one internal date is the last core grade by Mon 7 Dec (item 63).
>   The one registration is the protocol entries, made the moment the rehearsal checks pass.
> - An attended ticket starts from the `isc-build` commit it names; a factory run's base is the round-0 commit in its `factory.log`.
>   Cite functions by name, never by line number.
> - Integration is by script: the integration lane lands a pushed branch on `isc-build` only when the contract tests and the gate pass on the merged tree; a gate is green only with exit 0 and the last line `check: PASSED`.
>   Nobody merges by hand.
>   The plan's section 7 sets the landing order and the edit order of `orchestrator.py`, `runner.py` and `grader.py`.
> - A contract changes only through its owner (plan section 3).
>   Contract tests are frozen checks in docs/tickets/checks/contracts/; only the lead edits their open.txt, at landing.
> - Start no new item while landings wait longer than two gate runs.
> - The factory runs file tickets only, from the second clone `~/distbench-isc` on jhaveris.
>   Never use issue mode, never label an issue `ready-for-agent`, never run `next` there.
>   Run `bin/factory -C ~/distbench-isc lint <ticket>` (exit code) before release; the lead launches each run.
>   The launcher pushes each finished run as `build/f-<id>` and adds its row to the integration list.
>   A factory worker's own shell is always sandboxed; its done checks, which the supervisor runs, reach Docker and the full gate.
> - The build runs in a Claude Code session on jhaveris (item 50).
>   The lead's rule, Samyak's to overrule: a ticket written there takes an id J01 onward, uses this form and these blocks, gets a ledger row, and is committed on the build branch; a change to a ruling, a registered rule, a frozen check, money or a rental goes to Samyak first.
> - jhaveris: build sessions run with the sandbox off (item 31) and reach the gate by ssh.
>   Heavy work runs inside the build memory slice W04 sets up; until W04 lands, at most 2 factory runs and one MPI test at a time.
>   While calibration or confirmatory sessions run, the build slice is shrunk so the sessions' `memory` fits beside it; the orchestrator refuses a launch that does not fit (W13 part (i)).
>   Take locks with `flock` only, in the order gate, gpu, mpi (`gate-0.lock`, `gate-1.lock`, `gpu.lock`, `mpi-0.lock`, `mpi-1.lock` in `~/.local/state/distbench/`); never pkill by pattern.
>   A job that holds the GPU lock longer than 10 minutes runs only while no landing waits.
> - Done means the steps your item's Proven line names (plan section 5); a step proven on a stand-in stays marked UNVERIFIED.
> - Name the ledger ids this ticket closes and the trace ids its checks prove; the ledger and trace checks must pass from the end of batch 2.
> - Reviews: an attended ticket that changes code gets SESSION-PROTOCOL section 3a's two blind reviews of its branch against its base, Opus `code-review` at high and Codex read-only, unless its review box names `sam-cc-setup:lean-critic`; Codex read-only at every landing (use it freely, item 19); Fable blind and an Opus verifier at each batch end; `sam-cc-setup:lean-critic` on every ticket batch before release.
>   An Opus worker reproduces each finding before anyone fixes it.
> - pstack: before a non-trivial step, call the `sam-cc-setup:pstack` skill (a factory worker reads the router at the path its prompt gives) and follow the method it picks; name each pstack skill you used, and the decision it changed, in your report.
>   A ticket names a skill only to override the router's pick, on its "For this ticket:" line.
> - Push `isc-build` and `build/*` only, never `main`.
